coverage.main: Read the sixteen-page NDSS 2020 paper (DOI 10.14722/ndss.2020.24178; NDSS-hosted PDF): Sections I-VII including the FeatureFool attack, Algorithm 1, Tables I-III, Figures 1-5, experiments on five MLaaS platforms, defenses, limitations and references.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or linked; no arXiv version is listed in the corpus.
coverage.excluded_results: Adversarial examples (FeatureFool, PGD, CW, FA) are generated on local substitutes and used only as extraction queries; Table III and the ablations report substitute accuracy relative to the victim (extraction fidelity) and query budgets. The statement that malicious examples fool the local model with 100% success rate (Section IV) is white-box. The DefenseNet detection rate (Section VI) is a detection outcome. No transferred-evasion rate against a victim is reported.

f1.evidence: Victim and substitute clean accuracies are reported for extraction fidelity, not for any transfer-attack evaluation.

f3.evidence: Adversarial queries are not evaluated as transferred attacks.

f5.evidence: Perturbation settings for query generation are not transfer-attack budgets.

f6.evidence: No code is linked; with no transfer configuration this is neither a transfer recomputability success nor failure.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded the NDSS-hosted PDF and hashed it; the paper links only MLaaS platform pages and GitHub-collected test images, no code or data release.

bounds_exclusion.reason: No transferred misclassification rate against a victim model is reported.

limitations: Retained in the frozen corpus with non-applicability reasons; model-extraction fidelity is not an adversarial transfer outcome.
